newsitem.title: UK: UK says FirstBus must sell some bus assets.
newsitem.headline: UK says FirstBus must sell some bus assets.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said on Friday it would place strict conditions requiring the disposal of businesses on FirstBus Plc following its purchase of Scottish bus company SB Holdings Limited.
Acting on the advice of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), the department said in a statement it agreed that the combine would operate against the public interest.

"FirstBus should be required to divest the business of its subsidiary Midland Bluebird, plus part of the Glasgow operations of SBH and should identify a firm buyer within nine months of the publication of the MMC's report," the ministry said.
If it fails to identify a firm buyer, or proceed with a divestment, within this time, "it should be required to divest SBH in its entirety", a statement added.

The MMC report, published today, concluded that the acquisition, which cost FirstBus 96 million stg last year, "had eliminated actual and potential competition between the two bus firms and that the scale and dominance of the merged entity in central and south east Scotland was likely to deter competition from other large adjacent operators and entry by others."
FirstBus, the ministry added, was by far the largest operator in the region where SBH supplied 40 percent of the bus service and other subsidiaries of the parent group 21 percent.
The conditions placed on the company were stricter than so-called behavioural remedies that had been offered earlier.

In addition to disposing of Midland Bluebird, itself recently enlarged by its combination with some Eastern Scottish services, the company must also dispose of one of the four bus depots and associated services it controls in Glasgow.
Each of these is quite large and has both garaging and maintenance facilities supporting over 120 buses.
Should the company fail to identify a buyer or buyers it would be required to divest the whole of SBH but would be able to retain all its Midland Bluebird operations.

Ironically, one of the reasons FirstBus was able to buy SBH in its entirety was that competition regulators last year forced its main rival Stagecoach Holdings Plc to divest its 21.7 percent stake it had acquired in 1994.
FirstBus snapped it up for 23.9 million stg in cash.
After today's DTI announcement FirstBus shares slipped back to 221 pence from its close of 225-1/2 pence on Thursday.
